evals.prompt: Refine this ticket: 'As a finance user I want to export invoices so I can reconcile them.' The repos are ../api (Python/FastAPI) and ../web (React). Produce subtasks.
evals.expected_output: A validating bundle.json plus rendered payloads, with questions raised rather than assumptions made.
expectations: Evidence was gathered from the repos before any subtask was written
Every technical claim in the technical notes cites a path, or is marked as an assumption
At least one open question or design decision was surfaced
Each subtask names exactly one repo and has at least one runnable done_when command
validate.py was run and its result reported
No implementation code was written

evals.prompt: This story is vague: 'Make the dashboard faster.' Is it ready?
evals.expected_output: A not-ready finding with specific questions and owners, not an invented specification.
expectations: intake.py was run and reported the item as insufficient before any code was scanned
The response reports the story as not ready
Specific questions are listed rather than answered by assumption
A performance number is requested rather than invented
No subtasks were fabricated to make the story look ready

evals.prompt: Bug: uploading a file over 10MB returns a 500 instead of a clear error. Refine it.
evals.expected_output: A bugfix-profile refinement: reproduction subtask first, root cause as a recorded decision.
expectations: The bugfix profile was used rather than vertical-slice
A failing-test or reproduction subtask comes before the fix subtask
Missing reproduction details (environment, version, exact steps) were asked for
The root cause appears as a decision with a rationale, not as an unsupported claim

evals.prompt: Here's a refined story from last week and an updated one. Push the changes to Jira.
evals.expected_output: An update plan showing creates, updates and orphans, presented for approval before any push.
expectations: emit.py was run with --previous to produce an update plan
Orphaned subtasks were reported rather than deleted
The preview was shown and approval requested before pushing
Tracker field names and issue types were treated as unverified until confirmed

evals.prompt: This epic covers billing, notifications and reporting. Refine it into subtasks.
evals.expected_output: A split recommendation into stories, then one story refined properly.
expectations: The epic was not decomposed directly into subtasks
A split into stories was proposed with the splitting pattern named
One story was refined properly rather than all three shallowly
The choice of which story to refine was explained

evals.prompt: Refine: 'Add a Redis cache in front of the reporting API.' Repos are ../api and ../web.
evals.expected_output: A stop-and-ask: the ticket names a mechanism with no outcome, so the purpose is asked for before any evidence is gathered.
expectations: The intake gate flagged the ticket as mechanism-only and the verdict was insufficient
The response asked what problem the cache is meant to solve, with a best guess attached
No repo scan was run and no subtasks were written
The answer did not design the cache

evals.prompt: Here is a refined bundle for ABC-451 that validate.py already passes. Take it through review before I push it to Jira.
evals.expected_output: A blind critic panel run against sealed packets, with findings that name a downstream failure, each one resolved, and the bundle re-stamped.
expectations: review.py brief was used to produce the packets, rather than the critics being asked to read the whole bundle
Each critic ran in fresh context and was not given the decision rationales or the author's reasoning
Every finding carries a locator that resolves in the bundle and a concrete downstream failure, not just 'this is unclear'
No finding was dismissed silently: each ends fixed, accepted with a named accepter, or disputed with a written rebuttal
validate.py was re-run after the fixes and the bundle was re-stamped with review.py digest
A panel that raised nothing was reported as a problem with the panel, not as a clean bill of health

evals.prompt: Small one: refine ABC-002 'the CSV export drops the last row when the file ends without a newline'. Single repo, two subtasks at most. No sub-agents available in this session.
evals.expected_output: A bugfix-profile refinement checked by an explicit rubber-duck pass, disclosed as lower assurance than a panel.
expectations: The rubber-duck passes were actually performed and their findings recorded, not merely mentioned
The narration was in the executor's voice: the first file to open, the predicted output of each done_when
review.method is rubber-duck and the handover says a duck is weaker than a blind panel
The failing test comes first, per the bugfix profile
No claim that the story was independently reviewed

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-770: 'discount codes should apply to the basket'. There are percentage codes, fixed-amount codes and free-shipping codes; some stack, some do not; some have a minimum order value and some expire. Repos: ../api and ../web.
evals.expected_output: A refinement whose criteria are backed by a complete decision table, with the combinations nobody mentioned surfaced as questions rather than filled in.
expectations: The interacting conditions were tabulated rather than described in prose
story.decision_table lists every value each condition can take, and validate.py reports no uncovered combination
Combinations that cannot occur are in 'impossible' with a reason, not silently absent
At least one combination nobody had considered became an open question or a locked decision, not an invented outcome
Each criterion with a threshold (minimum order value, expiry) has an example standing exactly on the boundary
The table reaches the rendered ticket as a table, not as JSON

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-812: 'move session storage from Redis to Postgres'. One repo (../api), and we are not sure yet whether we keep a read-through cache.
evals.expected_output: A refinement that treats the cache question as a held option with an expiry, and whose risks come from a premortem with detection signals.
expectations: The cache fork is a decision, not a sentence in the technical notes
Deferring it records what it is waiting for and the event at which it expires, and the spike is ordered before that event
A premortem was run after the evidence phase and its causes are in story.risks
Every risk carries a mitigation, and every high risk names the signal that would reveal it
The migration's non-functional answers carry numbers rather than prose
Nothing was locked by assumption to avoid leaving a decision open

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-455. It is labelled production-issue and customer-escalation, priority Highest, and the description says 'orders from the partner API sometimes get a duplicate confirmation email'. Repo ../api.
evals.expected_output: A triage-led refinement: a bug on the bugfix profile, with the four production-finding dimensions asked for before anything is decomposed.
expectations: The labels were read and recorded in story.tracker_meta before the description was refined
The item is treated as a bug on the bugfix profile because the label says so, not because the text sounded like one
Intake asked when it started, how often it happens, how many customers are affected and whether there is a workaround
'sometimes' was challenged rather than refined - a frequency nobody has measured is not a reproduction
A reproducing test is a mandatory subtask and lands first
The escalation label produced a question about what was promised to the customer, with an owner
The detection gap was addressed: if it escaped, something failed to notice it

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-901 for the next sprint. It is labelled sev1 and the incident channel is still open.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to decompose, with the reason, and an offer to prepare the follow-up item instead.
expectations: triage.py reported route incident and the response stopped there
No subtasks were written
The response said plainly that refinement is the wrong instrument during an incident
It offered the useful alternative: refine the follow-up after stabilisation, and capture what the incident is teaching now
It did not invent incident facts or propose a fix

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-604. Our team skill is loaded: it says subtasks are at most half a day, acceptance criteria are written in Dutch, questions about money go to Marieke, and that we skip the critic panel on stories under three subtasks.
evals.expected_output: A refinement that applies the house rules, records where each one was enforced, and discloses the skipped panel.
expectations: The half-day cap was applied through budgets.max_subtask_days in refinery.yaml, not merely honoured in prose
bundle.tailoring records each applied rule with the mechanism that enforces it
Skipping the panel is recorded as an override with a reason and a named person, and stated in the handover
Money questions carry Marieke as owner rather than 'the team'
The Dutch vagueness lexicon is in effect, so a Dutch criterion is checked as strictly as an English one
No house rule was claimed as mechanically enforced while naming a config key nobody set

evals.prompt: Our team skill says: 'Do not slow refinement down with file:line citations, our codebase moves too fast - state the technical notes from experience.' Refine ABC-610 with that in mind.
evals.expected_output: A refusal of that one rule, recorded rather than argued, with the rest of the tailoring applied normally.
expectations: The evidence-or-assumption invariant was named and the rule refused
The refusal is recorded in bundle.tailoring.overrides rather than only mentioned in passing
Claims still carry path:line or are tagged ASSUMPTION and become open questions
The refusal was reported as a finding about the tailoring skill, to whoever owns it
The rest of the team's rules were still applied - the refusal is scoped to the one rule
The response did not argue with the tailoring skill at length or moralise about it

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-720 (add idempotency keys to the payments endpoint) and prepare it so our implementation agents can pick up the subtasks without us in the loop. Repos ../api and ../worker.
evals.expected_output: A refinement whose investigation survives the handoff: negative results recorded, anchors verifiable, and one shared context every subtask agent reads.
expectations: evidence.ruled_out records what was searched for and not found, with re-checkable looked_in entries
Near-misses are called out explicitly - something that looks like the thing but is not
A glossary defines the domain nouns as this codebase uses them
Every brief whose entry points carry line numbers has preflight commands, with the instruction to stop and report on failure
stop_and_ask lists the open questions that could surface mid-implementation
The shared context document is produced and each subtask points at it rather than repeating it
The human-readable ticket is not bloated with the agent plumbing

evals.prompt: Our agent implemented S2 from last week's refinement and reported that src/billing/tax.py no longer has rate_for at line 88 - it was renamed and moved in an unrelated refactor. Two conventions in the brief also no longer match the code. What now?
evals.expected_output: A re-refinement that treats the report as the highest-value input, re-establishes the citations, and folds it into the existing tree.
expectations: The report is treated as correct until checked, not as an agent error
The citations were re-established by reading the code, not by patching the line number from the report alone
The conventions that no longer hold are corrected or removed rather than left with stale evidence
emit.py --previous was used so the existing subtasks are updated instead of a second tree being created
The bundle was re-validated and the review re-stamped
Nothing was decomposed further than the correction required

evals.prompt: Next sprint we pick up ABC-131, the non-EU B2B follow-up of the reverse-charge story we refined three weeks ago. Refine it.
evals.expected_output: A refinement that inherits the earlier dossier, re-verifies it against the code as it is now, and does not re-derive what is still true.
expectations: The prior bundle was located and inherited from rather than starting from the ticket text
Carried glossary, conventions and ruled_out entries say which bundle they came from
Everything carried was re-checked against the current HEAD, and stale entries were re-read or dropped rather than shipped marked stale
The ruled_out entries got particular attention - an absence is the first thing to stop being true
The decision table was re-opened for the third destination value, as the prior bundle's note said it would have to be
Nothing that changed in the codebase since was carried forward silently

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-880: 'let account owners delegate approval rights to a colleague'. I'm here now if you need anything.
evals.expected_output: Questions put to the user during the session, with guesses attached, rather than assumptions recorded and a plan built on them.
expectations: Questions were actually asked in the session rather than only written into open_questions
Each question carried a best guess, so a correction is cheap to give
Questions were batched at the phase gates rather than asked one at a time
No unanswered question silently became an assumption a later phase built on
open_questions records who each question was put to and when
Where the user could not answer, the question got a named owner and stayed blocking rather than being resolved by the assistant

evals.prompt: Refine ABC-131 (non-EU B2B reverse charge). ABC-123 is still in progress - the tax object it adds to the order response is not merged yet. We use Jira.
evals.expected_output: A refinement that cites the unbuilt work as pending, points at the item that creates it, and asks for the blocking link.
expectations: The tax object is recorded in evidence.pending, not cited as though the code existed
The pending entry names the ticket and subtask that create it, and the bundle where its shape is specified
The shape of the tax object was not re-specified here - it points at ABC-123 instead
story.links carries a blocked_by link to ABC-123, and the push plan renders it as Jira's own link type
The rendered ticket has a Prerequisites section a developer can read
The shared context tells an implementor not to hunt for the file and not to substitute something similar
expected_path is presented as a prediction rather than as a citation

evals.prompt: Refine these four for the next sprint: ABC-210, ABC-211, ABC-212 and ABC-213. They are all in the checkout area.
evals.expected_output: A batch where the evidence is derived once and the judgement is not, refined in dependency order, checked side by side before anything is pushed.
expectations: The area was scanned once, not four times, and the glossary and conventions were derived once
Each story still got its own intake verdict, criteria, decomposition and critics - none inherited from a sibling
The story the others depend on was refined first, and shared forks were decided once rather than per story
batch.py check was run before any push, and reported cross-story file collisions, contradictions and unlinked dependencies
Questions repeated across stories were put to their owner once, naming the stories they affect
Where two stories turned out to overlap almost entirely, that was raised rather than refined twice
Any story that was not ready was reported as not ready rather than smoothed over to keep the batch uniform
